source_name: EU Building Stock Observatory June 2026 update
public_surface: technical building systems database and full XLSX download route
notes: The BSO officially covers installed technical building systems and was updated in June 2026, but this audit did not verify a Hungary-specific radiator/floor/wall/ceiling/fan-coil emitter distribution. BSO topic coverage is not itself emitter evidence.

source_name: KSH Household Budget and Living Conditions Survey questionnaire
notes: The questionnaire explicitly distinguishes gas convector; stove/fireplace/tile stove; electric storage heater; air conditioner; and electric floor/wall heating. It also records boiler/heat-pump heat generation. The public questionnaire defines categories but does not publish a complete emitter assignment.

Published national total primary-heating shares are 16.0% district heating, 6.3% building-central, 48.4% one-dwelling central and 28.9% individual fixed room heating. The table explicitly notes that one-dwelling central includes radiator/floor/wall heating and individual fixed includes convector/stove/fireplace, so it cannot identify emitter subtype.

source_name: KSH Census 2022 WBL011 heating and fuel joint
notes: P22 already materializes exact current heating-system topology over 116452 cells / 4008541 occupied dwellings. Census heating mode and fuel do not identify radiator/surface/convector/stove emitter subtype.

MEHI states that estimates indicate nearly 3 million outdated gas convectors and more than 800 thousand old gas boilers in residential buildings. These are equipment counts/context, not a dwelling-level emitter distribution and must not be converted into dwelling counts.

source_name: Official OENY e-tanusitas current certificate/document surface
source_scope: individual certified building or functional unit
public_surface: official certificate detail/template and address/HET public search
notes: Official e-epites guidance states that the detailed certificate contains current heating-system type and heat-emission mode such as radiator, and the official preview contains a dedicated photo-documentation slot for the characteristic heat emitter and its controls. The preview itself is synthetic and proves template capability only. Individual certificate evidence does not equal a complete occupied-stock emitter assignment, and the public surface does not prove a complete supply/return design-temperature assignment.

source_name: TÁRKI-REKK household energy survey published in REKK/BME gas-phaseout study
public_surface: public final report Figure 11 plus published questionnaire
notes: The weighted nationally representative survey has N=1013 overall; Figure 11 reports N=657 gas-heating households and exact device shares: traditional gas boiler 26.66%, condensing gas boiler 32.73%, gas convector 40.61%. Gas convector is a current emitter/device numeric control. Boiler shares are heat-generator controls and are not radiator evidence. The published overall 3.4% full-sample margin of error is not silently assigned to the N=657 conditional distribution.

source_name: TÁRKI-REKK full published household questionnaire emitter-boundary audit
public_surface: questionnaire appendix 7.1 Q18-Q20 Q32 Q50/Q50A Q67-Q69
notes: The full published questionnaire distinguishes heating topology and heat generators and contains radiator-related wording for thermostatic valves/cost allocators plus planned emitter-system modernisation. It does not ask a current hydronic radiator-vs-surface-heating-vs-mixed emitter-class question and does not ask design flow/return temperature. Q19 gas-convector remains valid direct device evidence; boiler cannot be converted to radiator.

source_name: HÉTFA / Habitat residential renovation impact study
notes: Public study URL https://hetfa.hu/wp-content/uploads/2022/09/HE%CC%81TFA_Tanulma%CC%81ny_Habitat.pdf. The report reuses KEOP/NÉER2 for typology, heat demand, carrier and heat-producer renovation scenarios. Text search of the public PDF yields no radiator/radiator-heating, floor-heating or heat-emitter stock distribution. Its low-temperature/condensing-boiler scenario tables are heat-producer assumptions, not current emitter prevalence or design-temperature observations.

source_name: BME Hungarian Residential Building Stock Model parametric analysis
source_scope: Hungarian residential archetype / EPC-derived model inputs
notes: The article provides an explicit stochastic uncertainty/sensitivity workflow and EPC-derived system characteristics, but the inspected archetype uses traditional gas-boiler heating and exposes heating-system-efficiency distributions rather than radiator/surface-heating/fan-coil prevalence. Useful inference framework != emitter population evidence.

The guide states that central heating is predominantly hot-water radiator heating with fewer floor/other surface-heating systems; it describes surface heating around 40 C and central radiator heating as the most widespread high-temperature solution. These are directional engineering statements only; no percentage or current-stock weight may be minted.

The official taxonomy separately codes floor heating, radiator heating and fan-coil installation. This proves current statistical category separability only. OSAP 1831 is construction-price statistics based on representative construction items; it does not publish national installation quantities, installed residential stock or emitter prevalence.

source_name: EHI Heating Market Report 2024 Hungary surface-heating penetration maps
notes: Screenshot-verified map colour places Hungary in the 33%-66% Medium Penetration band for both apartments and houses. This is surface-system presence, not an exclusive emitter share; it cannot be complemented into a radiator share because mixed systems and other emitters are not identified. Technology text gives 35/28 C surface-heating guidance and 55 C-or-lower modern-radiator guidance, but not Hungarian population weights.

source_name: EHI low-temperature emitter EPBD semantic authority
notes: EHI explicitly states that water temperature is a building/heating-system design and operating feature rather than an emitter-specific property. It also notes that operating temperatures vary with the heating curve and rarely equal design temperature. Used to retire national baseline temperature-distribution hunting as a mandatory stock input.

Field subset explicitly contains floor heating n=9 radiators n=14 and mixed radiator+floor systems n=23. Mean HP temperatures are 33.2 C floor 38.4 C mixed and 38.9 C radiator; heating curves overlap and mixed systems may be floor- or radiator-dominated. This validates transition-temperature modelling and mixed-system overlap semantics, not Hungarian shares.
